clue.text: Rock is what this one will do

definitions.text: Rock is what this one will do

parts.words: Rock is what this one will do
parts.note: a stone balanced so finely that a push sets it swaying back and forth, so rocking is its whole nature

explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish name for a balanced boulder that rocks when pushed, also called a rocking stone.

clue.text: Coming up a promenade, a beast of burden

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the words a promenade are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mall is a shaded public walk, a promenade

explanation.surface: A pack animal plods up the seafront walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' turns A MALL backwards, top to bottom becoming bottom to top in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid is kept as a pack animal in the Andes.

clue.text: Oliver's inadequate fare, fish — as punishment

parts.note: Oliver Twist famously asked for more of the thin workhouse porridge, gruel
a ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: The workhouse boy's meagre ration is fish, served as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a severe, exhausting ordeal, an old term for a harsh beating or penalty.

clue.text: Of course it's most refreshing

parts.note: on a golf course, the bar golfers reach after the eighteen holes is where they get a drink

explanation.definitionFit: Golfing slang for the clubhouse bar, visited after the last of eighteen holes.

clue.text: Note about Soviet Union containing nothing material

indicators.note: the note wraps around the rest of the wordplay, so about signals a container

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the Soviet abbreviation holds the zero inside it, as containing says

parts.note: USSR is the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A memo on the Soviet Union turns out to have no substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts O inside USSR, and 'about' wraps TE round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse brownish silk fabric from India, so a kind of cloth.

clue.text: One runs wild, thereby losing one's rights perhaps?

indicators.note: running wild suggests letters let loose to roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes off the rails and forfeits their rights as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs wild' rearranges ONE RUNS; the first two words do double duty in the surface but only as letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, failing to exercise a right can forfeit it, and the person who fails to exercise it is called this.

clue.text: Smith first in the race

explanation.definitionFit: The economist Smith who wrote The Wealth of Nations, and in Genesis the first man of humankind.

clue.text: Scandinavian is said to stoop

indicators.note: is said tells us the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a Dane is a native of Denmark, a Scandinavian

explanation.surface: A Norseman is reported to bend down.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend, lowering oneself to do something beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: Princess in the 27 — or Scots one rates in a harem perhaps?

indicators.note: the Scots word sits inside the jumbled harem letters
perhaps hints that a harem is only one possible order for these letters

parts.note: ane is the Scots form of one

explanation.surface: An Oriental princess, or perhaps a Scotswoman who ranks highly among a sultan's wives.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is the answer to 27-across, so the definition means a princess of the Orient. 'perhaps' jumbles A HAREM into MAHARE, and 'in' sets ANE inside it; 'rates' is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a maharajah, an Indian princess or queen.

clue.text: Birds performing sounded so exultant to the castaway

parts.note: robins are small songbirds
a performer is on, on stage

indicators.note: sounded asks for the spoken form of the following words

parts.note: to crow is to exult, so crowing so loudly gives crow so

explanation.surface: Singing birds sound joyful to a man marooned on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounded' makes CROW SO (exult so) into the surname of Defoe's hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's novel tells of a sailor shipwrecked alone on an island for years.

clue.text: A Scottish smoker joins students' union as an old boy

parts.note: a lum is a Scottish chimney, which smokes
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A Scotsman with a pipe signs up to the students' union as a former pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' suggests a person with a pipe but it is a chimney, LUM in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A former pupil or graduate of a school or college.

clue.text: Stone artefact represented the lion

indicators.note: represented means presented afresh, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A carved stone object depicts a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone tool from the New Stone Age.

clue.text: Cleansing rites — or remissions of sins? Not so

indicators.note: not so tells us to leave out the word so from what precedes it

parts.note: absolutions are formal pardons of sin by a priest

explanation.surface: Ritual washings, or the forgiving of sins, are queried.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual washings of the body, a religious purification.

clue.text: Sort of man one comes to stomach

definitions.text: Sort of man one comes to stomach

parts.words: Sort of man one comes to stomach
parts.note: the humorous phrase for one's appetite pairs this adjective with man, and one also goes to an inn

explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is a jocular term for the belly and its appetite.

clue.text: About to be a VIP in India

parts.note: C is circa, about
to live is to exist, to be

explanation.surface: Someone is about to become a big name on the subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Clive was the general who established British rule in Bengal.

clue.text: Artist swindles board

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A painter cheats the committee.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Dark Lady? Non-starter — no one backing, so going out

indicators.note: a non-starter loses its start, so the first letter goes

parts.note: an old, now offensive, term for a Black woman

indicators.note: backing means the words no one are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Dark Lady, with nobody supporting her, leaves the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-starter' drops the first letter of an old offensive word to leave EGRESS; 'backing' turns NO I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit or departure, a formal word for leaving.

clue.text: King turns up in one location as refugee from Egypt

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the reversed king is placed inside the word for a location

parts.note: a site is a location

indicators.note: in a down light turns up reads the king's name from bottom to top

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A monarch turns up somewhere as someone fleeing Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses LEAR to RAEL, and 'in' sets that inside SITE after I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrews of Exodus fled slavery in Egypt under Moses.

clue.text: Dark bird Hamlet might recognize when the wind's southerly?

definitions.text: Dark bird Hamlet might recognize when the wind's southerly?

parts.note: night is darkness

parts.words: bird Hamlet might recognize when the wind's southerly
parts.note: Hamlet says that when the wind is southerly he knows a hawk from a handsaw

explanation.surface: A night bird that the Danish prince could tell apart in a south wind.
explanation.definitionFit: An American nightjar that hunts insects at dusk.

clue.text: No good investment of course for capital orchestra in island group

indicators.note: the orchestra sits inside the island group

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off Galway in Ireland
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A bad bet on the course pays for London's orchestra to play in the islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means of a racecourse: a horse that fails to place is a poor bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that runs but is unplaced, so a betting loser.

clue.text: Egypt's old viceroy governor follows king to low joint

indicators.note: follows puts the governor after the king in the answer

parts.note: K is king in chess notation
HE is His Excellency, title of a governor
a dive is a disreputable bar

explanation.surface: A governor tags along after the king to a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Ottoman viceroys who ruled Egypt.

clue.text: Shark's part in Romeo and Juliet

explanation.definitionFit: A sluggish bottom-dwelling shark, and Juliet's garrulous carer in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: It's less than waist-high

indicators.note: less than means only part of the word waist-high is used, its tail end

explanation.surface: Something that sits below belt level.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper leg, which is below the waist.

clue.text: One' physician is a 'legendary Welsh giant

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is a mythical Welsh giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Idris was a giant of Welsh legend, whose seat is Cadair Idris in Snowdonia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh mountain bears the name of this giant astronomer of folklore.

clue.text: A flightless bird dashed round giving point to the attack

indicators.note: the word for dashed goes round the other pieces

parts.note: sped means dashed
the rhea is a large South American flightless bird

explanation.surface: An ostrich-like bird rushes round, sharpening an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading element of an offensive.

clue.text: "She — among the untrodden ways" (Wordsworth)

parts.note: fill in the missing verb from the opening line of a Lucy poem by Wordsworth

explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's line says she lived among untrodden ways.

clue.text: Criminal's food rejected by household god

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so food is read backwards

parts.note: grub is food
a lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A villain's dinner is turned down by the family deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A housebreaker is a kind of thief.

clue.text: Animate, at home, Arnold's Oxford dreamer

parts.note: in means at home
Matthew Arnold called Oxford the city of dreaming spires

explanation.surface: Stirring words from the poet's Oxford fantasist, spoken at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone with spirit or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Minimum loss of money in this quarter

indicators.note: loss of means the letter for money is dropped

parts.note: least means minimum
L is the pound sign, money

explanation.surface: The smallest financial loss in this district.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four compass points, quarters of the horizon.

clue.text: Prior's tenant in trouble, about to give up

indicators.note: the jumbled tenant goes around the word for give up
in trouble suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: to cede is to give up

explanation.surface: A monk's lodger in difficulty is about to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' scrambles TENANT to ANTENT, and 'about' puts it round CEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that came before, preceding.
